description: The conformance corpus for standards/085-security-baseline.md. Four parts. 'headers' is judged by applying response-headers.json to a response: each case names its class, the headers as sent (names case-insensitive), whether the OpenAPI document declares the endpoint public, and the exact set of findings a checker must report; an empty set is acceptance. Two cases are detectors: 'x-frame-options-without-frame-ancestors-rejected' fails a checker that lets X-Frame-Options satisfy the framing requirement, and 'hsts-without-include-subdomains-rejected' fails a checker that tests HSTS for presence and max-age alone. 'from-lines' is judged by running SB1's checker over a Dockerfile given as an array of lines: the findings are '<line number>:<finding>' and an empty list is acceptance; one case is a detector, 'second-stage-unpinned-rejected', which fails a checker that reads only the first FROM. 'scan-acceptance' is judged two ways: 'valid' by acceptance.schema.json (an 'entry' against #/$defs/entry, a 'file' against the whole schema), and where 'today' is given, by the calendar checks SB2 states: an entry past its expiry, and a window over ninety days, are findings. 'security-md' is judged by security-md.schema.json alone.

headers.why: SB3's document set in full: HSTS with includeSubDomains, the strict CSP with a per-response nonce and 'strict-dynamic', nosniff, referrer, the deny-list, COOP, CORP, and no-store because a nonced document cannot be cached.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3's API set in full: the inert CSP with sandbox, no-referrer, no-store on an authenticated response, and a Server header that is a product token with no version.
SB3's asset set: no CSP, no policy headers a static file cannot use, and the immutable cache form that is only correct because the name is the content hash.

SB3 admits the ordinary widenings: connect-src to the API origin under 060 AU7 topology B, img-src to data:, a nonce on style-src, CORP same-site, and preload on a domain its owner submitted. None of them touches script-src.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-Zm9vYmFyYmF6cXV4MTIzNDU2' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-Zm9vYmFyYmF6cXV4MTIzNDU2'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3, the detector: a year of max-age and no includeSubDomains. A cookie set on the apex reaches every subdomain, so one subdomain reachable in clear is the session in clear. A checker that tests HSTS for presence and a max-age alone accepts this set and fails only this case.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: a year is the preload list's floor and the rule's. A short max-age is a browser that forgets the site was HTTPS-only between visits.

SB3, the detector: X-Frame-Options DENY is present and frame-ancestors is not. Browsers consult frame-ancestors first and the superseded header never substitutes for it. A checker that treats DENY as satisfying the framing requirement accepts this set and fails only this case.
SB3: the superseded header sent beside the one that superseded it is harmless duplication and not a finding.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: no framing control at all. This is the sibling of the detector; every checker rejects it, which is what makes the detector a detector.

SB3: 'unsafe-inline' in script-src is the compatibility fallback for browsers that predate 'strict-dynamic', and it is a permission granted only to the clients least able to defend themselves. The nonce and 'strict-dynamic' are present, so this is the only finding.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic' 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: a host allow-list in script-src instead of a nonce. No nonce, no 'strict-dynamic', and a CDN origin that hosts something an attacker can load. Three findings, each a separate defect.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: a policy that only reports is a policy that is not enforced. Admitted during a rollout beside the enforced header, never instead of it.

headers.Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: a header every browser has removed support for, whose blocking mode introduced leaks of its own. Sent by a framework default, never by a decision.
SB3: a version in Server and a framework name in X-Powered-By are reconnaissance done for free. Two findings.
SB3: an authenticated response with a cache lifetime is one person's data in a shared cache. private does not redeem it; the rule is no-store.
SB3: the OpenAPI document declares this endpoint public and cacheable, so it states its own policy. The header must still be present.
SB3: with no Permissions-Policy every feature is available to every frame, the product's own included, so a compromised dependency can open the camera.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: camera=* grants the feature to every frame. (self) is admitted with a Conventions entry; * is never.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: a document with a cache lifetime is a document whose nonce will be stale on its second use; the shell is rendered per response and says so.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0mN0nc3ValueXYZ12345' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'

headers.why: SB3: an hour of max-age without immutable makes the browser revalidate a file whose name already proves its content; either the name is a hash and the file is immutable, or it is not this class.
SB3: default-src 'none' stops loads and frame-ancestors stops framing, but a browser navigated to the URL still renders the body in an origin with a cookie; sandbox is what makes it inert.

from-lines.why: SB1's canonical form: the digest is the pin, the tag is the version comment carried in-band, and an update tool maintains both as one edit.
SB1's admitted alternative: a bare digest with the version in a trailing comment, the way action pins are written.
SB1: a correct pin nobody can read, whose next update is a diff nobody can review.
SB1: a tag is a mutable pointer; the bytes it names change when upstream rebuilds and nothing in the repository changes when they do.
SB1: no tag is the latest tag, which is the most mutable pointer there is.
SB1's first exemption: scratch is the empty image and has no digest to pin.
SB1's second exemption: a FROM that names a stage this file declared with AS is pinned by that stage's own FROM.

SB1, the detector: the build stage is pinned and the runtime stage is not, so the image that ships is the unpinned one. A checker that reads only the first FROM accepts this file and fails only this case.
SB1: a reference the checker cannot read without evaluating the build is a pin nobody is checking.
SB1's third exemption: the --platform flag sits between FROM and the reference and does not change what is pinned.
SB1: a digest is sha256 plus 64 hex characters; a shorter one is not a content address.
SB1: Dockerfile instructions are case-insensitive, so a checker that only matches FROM in capitals would miss this line and pass an unpinned image.
SB1: a private registry with a port is an ordinary name; the tag after the last path component and the digest after it are what the grammar reads.

security-md.why: SB7 in full: a monitored channel, two numbers inside their ceilings, scope in and out, safe harbour stated, disclosure terms, and a security.txt with contact, expiry, policy and languages.
SB7: a commitment without a number is not a commitment.
SB7: three business days is the ceiling for telling a finder the report arrived.
SB7: a finder who fears the report will not send it; the section is required and the only value it admits is that the commitment is stated.
SB7: no channel is a public channel, because a finder who cannot find an address posts where they can.
SB7 through 020 IP4: RFC 9116 Expires is an instant, and the contract's timestamp form is RFC 3339 UTC with the pinned precision; a bare date does not match it.
